A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOS research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the new qualitative study in v3.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original detector-adaptation experiments, ablations, sensitivity studies, resource measurements, and results across object classes and detector backbones.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a qualitative comparison of MOS, SAR, and CoTTA in Appendix A.8 and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The warm-up, synergy-weighted checkpoint assembly, pseudo-label training, and model-bank replacement procedures remain unchanged. Equations (1)–(12) and Algorithm 1 retain the same method.

E1.justification: Both retain the same KITTI, KITTI-C, Waymo, and nuScenes transfer tasks, eight corruption types, and three object classes. Figure 9 illustrates the existing Waymo-to-KITTI task; its RGB image is reference-only.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged. The new qualitative comparison uses SAR and CoTTA, already evaluated on Waymo-to-KITTI; newly cited methods such as DPO are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, detector configurations, and adaptation settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 still specifies batch size 8, K = 5, and L = 112. The new visualization does not document a different evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A.8 adds a qualitative case study comparing localization and erroneous detections by SAR, CoTTA, and MOS in one illustrated scene. Existing ablations, sensitivity tests, and checkpoint analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–11 and existing performance plots are unchanged. Figure 9 adds qualitative evidence of spurious baseline detections and closer MOS box alignment. Appendix A.8 incorrectly calls background false positives 'false negatives'.

T1.justification: The synergy-weight derivation, generalized Gram matrix, similarity definitions, Hungarian matching formulation, and complexity argument remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about checkpoint synergy, adaptation coverage, and performance, including the 67.3% cross-corruption improvement. The shortened conclusion does not change their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of checkpoint diversity and knowledge retention, small-object pseudo-label limitations in A.5, and computational limitations remain unchanged. A.8 adds qualitative observations without a new mechanism explanation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the statement that code accompanies supplementary materials with an explicit GitHub repository address. This improves access information, although repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Implementation details in A.4 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including DPO, Tokens on Demand, DiPEx, and other detection/adaptation work, without substantially revising the positioning narrative. The existing TTA survey's preprint-to-journal update is bibliographic rather than a new cited work.

P1.justification: v3 adds A.8 and funding acknowledgments, updates author and conference-header information, and lightly condenses the conclusion. Most prose and section organization remain intact. A.6 incorrectly changes its Figure 8 reference to Figure 9.

P2.justification: Figure 9 adds a comparison of predicted and ground-truth boxes for SAR, CoTTA, and MOS, with an RGB reference image. Existing figures and tables retain their content and design, alongside limited repositioning and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The explicit code pointer and Figure 9 modestly improve reproducibility documentation and make comparative detection behavior inspectable. The quantitative study and method are unchanged. These gains are limited by A.8's false-positive/false-negative confusion and A.6's incorrect figure reference, but the additions remain useful.
